title: OpenAlternative Has 6.6K Stars And Zero Code
description:
OpenAlternative is the site people share when they want to stop paying for software. Its GitHub repo carries about six and a half thousand stars, so I cloned it expecting a Next.js directory app. There is no code in there at all. Four files: a license, a contributing guide, a funding file and a readme, and GitHub's own languages endpoint comes back empty. Their readme says why in one line. The repository was repurposed as a curated awesome-list, and the Next.js directory boilerplate that used to live there is now sold as Dirstarter. The cheapest tier is a hundred and fifty nine dollars. So the site that helps you stop paying for software now charges for its own code. The list itself still holds up, and that is the part worth keeping: 748 open source tools across eleven sections, published under CC0, free to copy into whatever you are building. One catch before you use it. All 1,027 entries link back to openalternative.co, never to the project's own repo, so you always land on their page first.

The directory: https://openalternative.co
